earlier_scan.note: Regular: final stress if consonant-final, penult if vowel-final (1sg verbs final)

new_statements.quote: There is only one rule for stress in Kotava, without any exceptions, other than verbs inflected for the 1st person singular. - Words ending in a semivowel or a consonant are stressed on the last syllable. Ex: tuvel, felay, sayakik - Words ending in a vowel are stressed on the penultimate syllable. Ex: blucte, kando, feralia - 1st person singular of the verbal conjugation, although ending in a vowel, is stressed on the last syllable by analogy with the rest of the verbal paradigm (characterised by final consonants), hence the diacritical mark. Ex: jin estú, jin lusteyé

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is fully predictable from the shape of the final syllable: a closed final syllable (ending in a consonant or the semivowel y/w) takes the stress; an open (vowel-final) final syllable is skipped and stress falls on the penult. The single morphological override is the 1sg verb form, which is vowel-final but stressed on the final syllable (written with an acute accent) by analogy with the other, consonant-final person forms. Segment-conditioned (closed-vs-open final syllable) with one morphological exception; the earlier scan_verify coded it 'segment+morphology-conditioned'.
new_statements.exceptions: Only the 1sg verb forms (vowel-final, stressed on the final syllable, marked by an optional acute accent). Proper nouns keep foreign spelling/diacritics but no stress statement is made for them.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level; no statement on phrase-level accent. The source is the language creator's prescriptive grammar, not an instrumental or descriptive study of speakers; Kotava is an a priori constructed language (created 1978 by Staren Fetcey).
new_statements.identity_note: Kotava is an a priori constructed auxiliary language (Staren Fetcey, 1978); the statement is the creator's/committee's prescriptive rule, identical in the English v. IV.03 (2016) and French v. IV.09 (2025) official grammars. No dialects; Glottolog lists no descriptive references beyond the ISO change request. Whether a constructed language belongs in the catalog is a scope decision for the caller.

sources.note: Phonology Ch. III 'STRESS [bloskara]' pp. 6-7: one exceptionless rule — words ending in a consonant or semivowel are stressed on the last syllable; words ending in a vowel on the penultimate; 1sg verb forms (vowel-final) are stressed on the last syllable by analogy with the consonant-final verbal paradigm and carry an acute accent.
Second-hand restatement: final stress if consonant-final, penult if vowel-final, 1sg verbs final with acute accent; links both official grammar PDFs. This was the earlier scan's source.
Second-hand and partly garbled (says 'accent grave' where the grammar says acute); same three-part rule.
